prompt:
This project has a Makefile, a tab separated data file data/products.tsv (columns sku, name, category, price_cents, stock, note), a lookup file data/categories.tsv (columns category, label) and small Python tools in tools/ (read their docstrings; do not change them). Make these changes.

Data file, data/products.tsv, rewritten in place:
- Rename the column price_cents to price and write its values in dollars with exactly two decimals: 1999 becomes 19.99, 5 becomes 0.05, 100000 becomes 1000.00, 123456789 becomes 1234567.89 (no thousands separators). A row whose price_cents is empty keeps an empty price.
- Add a column named label directly after category. Its value is the label that data/categories.tsv gives for the row's category (matched exactly). A category that has no line in data/categories.tsv gets the label unlabeled. data/categories.tsv comes from a Windows export and uses CRLF line endings: do not change that file, and no label in products.tsv may contain a carriage return.
- Add a column named value directly before the last column: price times stock in dollars with exactly two decimals (a row with price_cents 250004 and stock 59 gets 147502.36, stock 0 gives 0.00). It is empty when the price is empty.
- Add a last column named status: out when stock is 0, low when stock is from 1 to 9, ok when stock is 10 or more.
- The columns are now sku, name, category, label, price, stock, note, value, status. Every other field stays exactly as it is, including empty fields (a row whose note is empty still has its tab, so the row has 9 fields with two tabs in a row before the value) and names with quote or non ASCII characters. The rows keep their order. The file keeps LF line endings and exactly one newline at the end.

Makefile:
1. Change the stats target so it reports on the price column instead of price_cents.
2. Change the COLUMNS variable to 9 so make check expects the new column count.
3. Change the clean target so it removes $(DIST) as well as $(OUT).
4. Add the target $(OUT)/lowstock.tsv with prerequisites $(DATA) and $(OUT). Its recipe runs tools/tsvfilter.py to write the header and the rows whose status is low or out to that file.
5. Add the target $(OUT)/categories.txt with prerequisites $(DATA) and $(OUT). Its recipe writes the sorted, unique category names, one per line, to that file, using tools/tsvcolumn.py and sort -u.
6. Add the target $(OUT)/labels.txt with prerequisites $(DATA) and $(OUT). Its recipe writes the sorted, unique label values, one per line, to that file, the same way as for the categories.
7. Add the target $(OUT)/value_stats.txt with prerequisites $(DATA) and $(OUT). Its recipe runs tools/tsvstat.py on the value column and writes its output to that file.
8. The recipes of the four targets in items 4 to 7 write their output to $@ and do not repeat the path of the output file (for example do not write build/labels.txt in the recipe).
9. Add the phony target dist with the prerequisites stats, $(OUT)/value_stats.txt, $(OUT)/lowstock.tsv, $(OUT)/categories.txt and $(OUT)/labels.txt, in that order. Its recipe creates $(DIST) with mkdir -p and then runs tools/bundle.py to write $(DIST)/bundle.txt from $(OUT)/stats.txt, $(OUT)/value_stats.txt, $(OUT)/lowstock.tsv, $(OUT)/categories.txt and $(OUT)/labels.txt, in that order. Add dist to .PHONY.
10. Change the all target so its prerequisites are stats, check and dist, in that order.

Use the existing variables (PYTHON, DATA, OUT, DIST) in the new targets instead of writing paths in full, so make OUT=other DIST=other2 dist works. Every recipe line must start with a tab character, and the other lines of the Makefile must stay as they are. The Makefile is checked with a small stand in for make, so keep to the simple style it already uses (variables, $(NAME), $@, $<, $^, explicit rules, .PHONY) and do not use pattern rules, make functions, include or conditionals. Recipes are run with sh and the checks run with LC_ALL=C, so sort -u orders by byte value.
